title: Conrad et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery (Case #1)
disposition_detail: Issue 1 (May the Session dissolve the official relationship between the church and all ruling elders, without censure, when requested by the congregation?) answered affirmative. Issue 2 (May the Session concur and request Presbytery to appoint a Commission as interim Session?) answered affirmative. The complaint is therefore not sustained. TE Morton Smith's constitutional inquiry concerning Judgment 1 was denied. TE Charles L. Wilson's separate objection was ordered spread on the minutes; dissenters signed it, but it was not adopted. SJC approval: 21 concurring, 3 abstentions.
first_summary: The SJC answered two questions about a session's dissolution of its ruling elders and request for an interim session. It said a session may dissolve the official relationship with all ruling elders when a congregational majority asks, because BCO 24-6b extends by good and necessary deduction to multiple identified elders. Such action does not divest office. BCO 13-9 and 15-2 allow an interim session. The complaint was denied; a constitutional inquiry was also denied.
summary: Can a session dissolve the official relationship between the church and all its ruling elders, and request an interim session, when a congregational majority asks it to do so? The SJC answered both issues yes. It held that BCO 24-6b's provision for an elder/congregation dissolution extends by good and necessary deduction to identified elders collectively, and that such action removes the official relationship without censure but does not divest the elder's office. BCO 13-9 and 15-2 authorize the interim session. The complaints failed; Smith's constitutional inquiry was denied. 21 concurred, 3 abstained.
